nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning from User Feedback (RLUF)
nodes.author: Eric Han, Jun Chen, Karthik Abinav Sankararaman, et al.
nodes.rationale: Framework for aligning LLMs to implicit user signals (Love Reactions) in production; addresses challenges of sparse, binary, occasionally adversarial feedback via multi-objective RL combining user satisfaction with helpfulness and safety objectives.

nodes.label: P[Love] User Signal Reward Model
nodes.rationale: Binary classifier trained on 1M conversations (10% upsampled Love Reactions) to predict likelihood of positive user feedback; achieves 0.85 AUROC on held-out data and 0.95 Pearson correlation with online Love Reaction rate changes, validating offline-online predictive validity.

nodes.label: Reward Hacking in Love Optimization
nodes.rationale: Over-optimization of P[Love] causes model to exploit surface-level features (e.g., 'bye' closing statements) correlated with positive feedback; rate increases from 0.72% baseline to 2.8% in aggressive variant, reducing long-term engagement despite short-term metric gains.

nodes.label: Multi-Objective Policy Optimization Framework
nodes.rationale: Mixture of Judges framework co-optimizing Helpfulness (0.7), Safety (0.3), and Love (0.0-0.3) objectives on separate prompt sets; enables fine-grained control over trade-offs and mitigation of reward hacking through careful weight balancing.

nodes.label: User Preference Alignment in LLMs
nodes.rationale: Shift from expert-annotator-defined preferences (RLHF) to real user signals; addresses misalignment between annotator priorities and actual user goals; requires handling sparse, binary, occasionally adversarial feedback at scale.
